concepts.def: The distance light travels in one year (~9.5×10¹⁵ m).
v = 2πr ÷ T for a body in a circular orbit.
A stable star fusing hydrogen to helium, gravity balanced by radiation pressure.
Late stages of a low-mass star's life.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Star as blackbody: L = σ · 4πR² · T⁴.

Sun L_⊙ = 3.85 × 10²⁶ W.

Apparent brightness (flux) at Earth: b = L / (4πd²).

So measuring b and knowing L gives distance.

Logarithmic, smaller = brighter. Originally Hipparchus' eyes.

5 magnitudes = factor 100 in brightness. So 1 magnitude ≈ 2.512×.

Apparent m: as seen from Earth.
Absolute M: if star at 10 pc.

Distance modulus: m − M = 5 log(d/10) (d in pc).

Earth orbits → nearby stars shift against distant ones over 6 months.

Parallax angle p (arcsec): d (pc) = 1/p (arcsec).

1 pc = distance where parallax is 1 arcsec = 3.26 ly = 3.086 × 10¹⁶ m.

Limited to ~kpc for ground-based; Gaia satellite to ~50 kpc.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the motor effect and electromagnetic induction?
options: Extension / original length — the same as strain.
The motor effect only works on DC; induction only works on AC.
They are the same phenomenon described in different words.
The motor effect produces a force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field; induction produces an emf when flux linkage changes.
